To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

maternal severity of IPV exposure is associated with PTSD diagnosis, maternal IPV PTSD is in turn associated with attachment disturbance in children, and maternal methylation status at the HTR3AR gene is linked to maternal and child aggression, and to decreased medial pre-frontal cortical activity in relation to IPV exposure.
the severity of maternal exposure to interpersonal violence was associated with the diagnosis of maternal post-traumatic stress disorder (PSTD).

maternal IPV PTSD was associated with disturbed child secure base behavior and that HTR3A DNA methylation was associated with IPV PTSD severity, maternal aggressive behavior, and child secure base disturbance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of early adversity and trauma exposure on child development and the mechanisms by which these exposures may influence brain and behavior.
the role that serotonin 3A receptors play in the development of child aggression.
the role of epigenetic processes in the intergenerational transmission of trauma and psychopathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the methylation of the HTR-3A gene in the mother is linked to her severity of exposure to interpersonal violence, her post traumatic stress disorder, her aggressive behavior and the disturbed attachment of her child.
maternal severity of IPV exposure is associated with maternal PTSD which is in turn associated with maternal aggression and child disturbance of attachment.
maternal IPV and maternal PTSD are linked to HTR3A CpG2_3 methylation, maternal AgB, and disturbed child attachment in the form of self-endangering behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maternal exposure to IPV is linked to maternal PTSD, which in turn is linked to disturbed attachment and self-regulation in the child.

maternal IPV exposure is associated with increased methylation of the HTR 3A gene and increased maternal PTSD, aggressive behavior and disturbed maternal child relationships and that the methylation is associated with decreased medial frontal cortical activity in response menacing relational film clips and increased self endangering behavior in the child.
the methylation of serotonin receptor 1A and 3A genes is linked to child attachment disturbance and self-endangering behavior in the context of maternal IPV and PTSD.
The main takeaway from our work is that

HTR3A CpG2_iii methylation is associated with both maternal IPV exposure and child self endangering behavior, and that HTR3a methylation is also associated with decreased mPFC activity in response to threatening relational stimuli.

the methylation status of the serotonin 2A receptor gene is associated with maternal IPV exposure and maternal IPV related psychopathy and that this methylation status is in turn associated with decreased medial frontal cortical activity in response menacing relational stimuli and child attachment disturbance.
maternal HTR3A DNA methylation is associated with maternal IPV related psychpathology, trauma induced neural activation, and child disturbance in attachment.
